descriptor: Packaging manufacturer/distributor (Flexibles & Specialty Packaging) · FY ends 30 June · reported in AUD · in voluntary administration since 23 Oct 2025 — businesses sold to KnoxCorp subsidiaries; administrator has stated no return to shareholders is expected

charts.title: Operating Cash Flow, CapEx & Lease Principal Repaid

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Pro-Pac Packaging Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Pro-Pac Packaging Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Pro-Pac Packaging Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Pro-Pac Packaging Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Pro-Pac Packaging Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Pro-Pac Packaging Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow, CapEx and lease principal
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets; lease principal repaid is the AASB16 financing outflow for the plant, equipment and site leases the manufacturing footprint runs on.

For Pro-Pac Packaging Limited: leases were a fixed, recurring cash cost of roughly A$9m/year through FY2024 regardless of volume -- a drag that compounded the revenue declines which tipped the business into administration.

What to watch:

  • CapEx and lease outflows rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Pro-Pac Packaging Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

ebitdaBridge.title: Statutory vs underlying EBITDA
ebitdaBridge.content:
Statutory EBITDA is reported as-is; underlying EBITDA excludes significant items (impairments, restructuring, redundancy and other one-off charges) that management treats as non-recurring.

For Pro-Pac Packaging Limited: the gap is large and recurring, not a single bad year -- FY2024 statutory EBITDA of -A$21.3m versus underlying A$4.4m, and FY2019 and FY2022 show the same pattern. Significant items turned sharply more negative into 1H FY2025 (-A$24.4m) just before the strategic review, ASX suspension and voluntary administration in late 2025.

What to watch:

  • Whether "non-recurring" items keep recurring -- a tell that the underlying business is weaker than adjusted figures suggest
  • The size of the gap relative to statutory EBITDA itself

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue: Flexibles vs Specialty Packaging
segmentRevenue.content:
Flexibles is in-house film manufacturing (stretch/shrink wrap, silage wrap, fresh produce bags, barrier/lidding films), roughly 78% of revenue; Specialty Packaging is sourced and distributed specialty packaging and consumer products, roughly 22%.

For Pro-Pac Packaging Limited: both segments were declining into FY2025 -- Flexibles fell from A$143.4m to A$108.6m and Specialty Packaging from A$39.9m to A$34.2m across 1H FY2023-1H FY2025 -- with a collapse in volume from one concentrated Middle East customer hitting Flexibles hardest. FY-only totals are not disclosed in the filings extracted to date, so this chart shows the half-year splits.

What to watch:

  • Whether one segment is declining faster than the other (mix shift)
  • Customer concentration risk within Flexibles

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Pro-Pac Packaging Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Pro-Pac Packaging Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
